headline: Rates Hold Steady as Markets Wait on the Fed
tileReason: The daily 30-year average held at 7.33% Monday, and with oil easing and the Fed's two-day meeting starting today, bonds are mostly treading water this morning.
takeaway: Mortgage rates went nowhere on Monday. The daily 30-year average held at 7.33%, the same as Friday and still close to its lowest level in a month. Bond markets had a quiet day: tech stocks bounced back, which normally pulls money out of bonds, but oil prices slipped for a second day and offset it. This morning brings a mixed picture. Brent crude is down about 1% to roughly $114 to $115 a barrel after Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials met with Iran's leaders and agreed to keep talking, and cheaper oil eases inflation worries. On the other side, the morning's U.S. reports came in stronger than expected: consumer confidence jumped to 91.7 from 84.2, new home sales beat forecasts at a 676,000 yearly pace, and core factory orders rose. A sturdier economy tends to nudge rates up. Net result: the 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates tend to follow, is hovering around 4.97% to 5.00%, roughly unchanged, so lender pricing looks flat for now. The Federal Reserve (the Fed, the central bank) began its two-day meeting today and announces its decision Wednesday at 2:00 PM ET. Markets see roughly a 9 in 10 chance it holds steady, but about an 80% chance of a hike in December, so Chair Warsh's tone matters more than the decision itself. Thursday's PCE inflation report and first look at third-quarter growth are the next big tests. Over the next month the odds look close to balanced, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via SEE News/Reuters (Oct 27) and FXEmpire (Oct 26); Trading Economics (Oct 23); Quartz (Oct 27)
fedOdds.note: CME FedWatch put the chance of a hike on October 28 at about 11% on Tuesday (SEE News, citing Reuters), up slightly from about 9% Monday morning (FXEmpire), so roughly 89% to 91% for a hold. December is a different story: FedWatch shows about 82% for a hike (Reuters via SEE News, Oct 27), Quartz says better than 80%, and Trading Economics had about 76% on Friday. The Fed is in its quiet period, so no official comments are expected before Wednesday's 2:00 PM ET statement.

drivers.title: Oil slips again on Gulf diplomacy
drivers.text: Brent crude settled about $0.90 lower Monday near $115.80 and slipped about another 1% early Tuesday to roughly $114.70, after officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan met Iran's leaders and agreed to keep talking. Cheaper energy eases fears that inflation will stay high, so bond investors accept slightly lower yields, which helps mortgage rates. Houthi drone attacks on Saudi Arabia are continuing, so this relief could reverse quickly.

drivers.title: Stronger U.S. data this morning
drivers.text: Consumer confidence jumped 7.5 points to 91.7 in October, new home sales ran at a 676,000 yearly pace versus about 650,000 expected, and business equipment orders outside transportation rose 0.5%. When the economy looks sturdier, investors expect the Fed to stay tough on inflation and are less eager to own bonds, which nudges yields and mortgage rates up. Consumers' one-year inflation expectations eased but remain high at 5.8%.

drivers.title: Fed meeting underway, December hike in view
drivers.text: The Fed's two-day meeting started today. Markets expect it to hold its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% on Wednesday but see about an 80% chance of a hike in December after hot September inflation. That expectation keeps a floor under bond yields and mortgage rates. If Chair Warsh sounds more worried about inflation than expected, rates could rise; if he sounds patient, they could ease.

drivers.title: Tech stocks bounce, but bonds hold their ground
drivers.text: Tech shares rallied Monday, with chip stocks leading and the Nasdaq 100 up about 1%. When stocks recover, some of the safe-haven money that poured into bonds last week tends to leave, which pushes yields up. This time bonds held steady, which suggests last week's rate improvement has some staying power. Microsoft and Alphabet report earnings Wednesday, so this tug-of-war may continue.

drivers.title: Mortgage rates are still unusually far above Treasuries
drivers.text: The daily 30-year average is running about 2.3% above the 10-year Treasury yield, compared with a more typical 2.0%. That extra cushion means mortgage rates have room to improve if markets calm down, even without a further drop in Treasury yields.

outlook.basis: It's close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are. Working in borrowers' favor: oil is backing off on talk of Gulf diplomacy, nervous tech stocks can send money into bonds on short notice, and mortgage rates are still unusually far above the 10-year Treasury (about 2.3% vs. a typical 2.0%). Working against them: a December Fed hike is still widely expected, September inflation ran hot, this morning's data showed a sturdier economy than forecast, and oil remains above $100 with attacks on Saudi targets continuing. Big swing events: the October 28 Fed decision, the October 29 PCE inflation and GDP data, the November 3 midterm elections, the November 6 jobs report, the November 10 CPI report, and any escalation in the Gulf.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.33%, close to a one-month low and down from roughly 7.5% in early October. The Fed decides Wednesday and key inflation data lands Thursday, so the next few days could bring bigger swings than usual; it's worth asking your lender how locking now, a float-down option, or waiting would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: New home sales beat forecasts in September, so resale homes are still competing with builders for a limited pool of stretched buyers. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to lower their rate, can help a home stand out while rates sit near a one-month low.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Mortgage rates are holding steady around 7.33%, near a one-month low, as markets wait on Wednesday's Fed decision and Thursday's inflation data.
